The elections coincided with the [[2022 Nebraska gubernatorial election|Nebraska gubernatorial election]], as well as other elections to the [[2022 United States House of Representatives elections|U.S. House of Representatives]], [[2022 United States Senate elections|elections]] to the [[United States Senate|U.S. Senate]], and various [[2022 United States elections|state and local elections]]. The incumbent was Republican [[Mike Flood (politician)|Mike Flood]], who was elected with 52.7% of the vote in a [[2022 Nebraska's 1st congressional district special election|2022 special election]] after the previous incumbent, [[Jeff Fortenberry]], resigned March 31, 2022, after having been indicted and convicted on charges of lying to the FBI about campaign donations.{{cite web |title=General Election Official Results |url=https://sos.nebraska.gov/sites/sos.nebraska.gov/files/doc/elections/2020/2020-General-Canvass-Book.pdf |website=Nebraska Secretary of State |access-date=December 4, 2020}} === Republican primary === ==== Candidates ==== ===== Nominee ===== * [[Mike Flood (politician)|Mike Flood]], incumbent U.S. representative{{Cite web|last=Walton|first=Don|date=January 16, 2022|title=Flood challenges Fortenberry, says indictment puts House seat at risk|url=https://journalstar.com/news/state-and-regional/govt-and-politics/flood-challenges-fortenberry-says-indictment-puts-house-seat-at-risk/article_d2c49949-faa5-5f80-a9d7-8bb3eb7b7e9e.html|url-status=live|access-date=January 16, 2022|website=[[Lincoln Journal Star]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220116230919/https://journalstar.com/news/state-and-regional/govt-and-politics/flood-challenges-fortenberry-says-indictment-puts-house-seat-at-risk/article_d2c49949-faa5-5f80-a9d7-8bb3eb7b7e9e.html |archive-date=January 16, 2022 }} ===== Eliminated in primary ===== * Thireena Yuki Connely, teacher * Curtis D.
